senses.definition: (uncountable) Synonym of porcelain, a hard white translucent ceramic made from kaolin, now (chiefly US) sometimes distinguished in reference to tableware as fine or good china.

examples: ...a Present of certain very rich Pieces of China.
He set the table with china, cloth napkins, and crystal stemware.
The traditional 20th anniversary gift is china.

quotes.text: They sell Callicoes, Cheney Sattin, Cheney ware.
quotes.reference: 1634, Thomas Herbert, A Relation of Some Yeares Trauaile, Begunne Anno 1626. into Afrique and the Greater Asia, page 41:

senses.definition: (uncountable, chiefly US, dated) Cheaper and lower-quality ceramic and ceramic tableware, distinguished from porcelain.

quotes.text: What is porcelain? A fine earthenware differing from china in being harder, whiter, harder to fuse and more translucent than ordinary pottery.
quotes.reference: 1921 May 11, “Edison Questions Stir Up a Storm”, in New York Times:

senses.definition: (uncountable) Synonym of China root, the root of Smilax china (particularly) as a medicine.

quotes.text: China, saith Manardus, makes a good colour in the face, takes away melancholy, and all infirmities proceeding from cold […].

senses.definition: (uncountable, obsolete) Synonym of cheyney: worsted or woolen stuff.

quotes.text:
...And then the last boon I'll implore,
Is to bless us with China so tight...

senses.definition: (countable) Synonym of China rose, in its various senses.

quotes.text: Rosa indica (the common China); Rosa semperflorens (the monthly China).

senses.definition: (countable, Cockney rhyming slang, Australia, South Africa) Synonym of mate (rhyme of china-plate).

quotes.text: ‘Now, then, my china-plate...’ This is essentially a brick~layer's phrase. If for ‘china-plate’ you substitute ‘mate’,[…] the puzzle is revealed.

senses.definition: (uncountable, dated) Tea from China, (particularly) varieties cured by smoking or opposed to Indian cultivars.
(countable, games, chiefly US, obsolete) A glazed china marble.

quotes.text: The marbles, in those days, had their primitive names. The unglazed china ones were called plasters because they looked like plaster; the glazed china marbles were called chinas. I remember how charming were the partly colored lines which encircled them.

senses.definition: (countable, music) A kind of drum cymbal approximating a Chinese style of cymbal, but usually with Turkish influences.

quotes.text: China cymbals are a type of short sound cymbal. [Brand X] makes chinas with really short sounds.
